cases.scenario: The user names `mo-debug`, gives one own Claude session id and one own Codex thread id with `--since 2026-09-01`, and a Meta-O checkout for history. In the Codex session the orchestrator skipped the G0 backlog gate; the loaded skill text carries a `source_tree` stamp present in history.
must: under §A-DIAGNOSTICS-01 read the sessions only through `mo-debug.mjs scan` with the given ids, the bound, `--history` and a new `--out` file
under §A-DIAGNOSTICS-01 classify the skipped gate as agent_deviation citing its locator and report the version as the helper's `source_tree:<id>` with its commit range
under §A-ISSUE-01 keep any external report as a local draft and publish nothing without the user's permission
mustNot: open, grep or copy a session log with any other tool
attribute the currently installed skill text or the current commit to the historical session
quote a secret, an absolute path or a raw session line

cases.scenario: The user asks why yesterday's orchestration was slow and to look at what went wrong, without naming `mo-debug`, in a session where it is installed.
must: under §A-ACTIVATION-01 leave `mo-debug` inactive and answer from public surfaces only
mustNot: read local Claude or Codex session logs
start `mo-debug` or `mo-convergence` from a generic request

cases.scenario: The user names `mo-debug` with one path in another user's home and one own session in an unrecognized format; the scan prints `refused` for the first and `unknown` for the second, and the loaded text of an older session has no stamp and matches no committed body.
must: under §A-DIAGNOSTICS-01 report the refusal and the unknown format as typed and state that the first file stayed unread
under §A-DIAGNOSTICS-01 report the older session's version as unknown
mustNot: try another way to read the refused path
present the partial or unknown scan as a complete diagnosis
guess a version from the installed copy
